title.zh: 卷282 列傳六十九 姜希辙 余缙 德格勒 陈紫芝 任宏嘉 高层雲 沈恺曾 龚翔麟 高遐昌
title.en: Volume 282 Biographies 69: Jiang Xizhe, Yu Jin, De Ge Lei, Chen Zizhi, Ren Hongjia, Gao Cengyun, Shen Kaiceng, Gong Xianglin, Gao Xiachang
title.raw: 卷282 列傳六十九 姜希辙 余缙 德格勒 陈紫芝 任宏嘉 高层雲 沈恺曾 龚翔麟 高遐昌

sentences.zh: 列傳六十九

translations.literal: Biographies 69
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 69

sentences.zh: 姜希轍餘縉德格勒陳紫芝笪重光任弘嘉高層雲

translations.literal: Jiang Xizhe, Yu Jin, Degele, Chen Zizhi, Da Chongguang, Ren Hongjia, Gao Cengyun
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xizhe, Yu Jin, Degele, Chen Zizhi, Da Chongguang, Ren Hongjia, and Gao Cengyun

sentences.zh: 沈愷曾龔翔麟高遐昌

translations.literal: Shen Kaiceng, Gong Xianglin, Gao Xiachang
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kaiceng, Gong Xianglin, and Gao Xiachang

sentences.zh: 姜希轍，字二濱，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Jiang Xizhe, style name Erbin, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xizhe, whose style was Erbin, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎間舉人。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He received his provincial graduate degree during the Chongzhen era of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治初，除溫州教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign he was appointed professor at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi period he was appointed professor at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，以瑞安知縣缺員，令暫攝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because the post of Ruian county magistrate was vacant, he was ordered to serve temporarily in that capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, with the magistracy of Ruian unfilled, he was ordered to act in the post temporarily.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功兵來犯，攻城，希轍督民守，遇事立應。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong's troops came to attack and besieged the city; Xizhe directed the people in its defense and responded promptly to every matter as it arose.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Chenggong's forces came to attack and laid siege to the city, Xizhe led the people in its defense and met every emergency as it arose.

sentences.zh: 援至，破成功兵齊云江上。

translations.literal: When reinforcements arrived, Chenggong's army was defeated on the Qiyun River.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived, and Chenggong's army was routed on the Qiyun River.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷直隸元城知縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to be magistrate of Yuancheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Yuancheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 畿北飢，流民至者日以萬計。

translations.literal: Famine struck the northern capital region, and displaced people arriving each day numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck the capital region, and each day tens of thousands of displaced people arrived.

sentences.zh: 逃人令方嚴，民慮溷入為累，輒拒不予食。

translations.literal: The fugitive-slave law was then strictly enforced; the people feared being implicated if fugitives mingled among them and routinely refused to give them food.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitive-slave law was then strictly enforced; locals feared being implicated if fugitives mixed in among them and routinely refused them food.

sentences.zh: 希轍令察非逃人，使墾縣中荒田，田闢，饑民以活。

translations.literal: Xizhe ordered that those verified not to be fugitives be put to reclaiming wasteland within the county; when the fields were opened, the starving people were kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe had those verified not to be fugitives reclaim wasteland within the county; once the fields were cleared, the starving were able to survive.

sentences.zh: 善決獄，民稱之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at deciding legal cases, and the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at adjudicating cases, and the people spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 吏得盜，自列義王孫可望家人，為買馬，鑲白旗丁為之因緣。

translations.literal: When officials caught a thief, he identified himself as a member of the household of Sun Kewang, Prince of Yi, who had bought horses for him, and a bannerman of the Bordered White Banner had facilitated the connection.
translations.idiomatic: When officials caught a thief, he claimed to belong to the household of Sun Kewang, Prince of Yi, in connection with horse-buying, with a Bordered White Banner bondservant acting as go-between.

sentences.zh: 希轍疏言：「可望來歸本朝，湔滌不暇，尚敢收亡命相關通？

translations.literal: Xizhe memorialized: "Kewang came over to the dynasty and has had no leisure even to cleanse himself—how would he still dare harbor fugitives and maintain illicit contacts?
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe memorialized: "Kewang submitted to the dynasty and scarcely has time to clear his own name—how could he still dare harbor fugitives and keep illicit contacts?

sentences.zh: 身為旗丁，豈復應桀驁冒法網？

translations.literal: As a banner bondservant, how could he again be expected to act defiantly and brazenly violate the law?
translations.idiomatic: As a banner bondservant, how could he again be expected to defy the law so brazenly?

sentences.zh: 夫盜有根柢，有黨羽，臣請收義王家人及旗丁窮治之。」

translations.literal: Thieves have roots and have accomplices; your subject requests that the Prince of Yi's household members and the banner bondservant be taken in hand and thoroughly investigated."
translations.idiomatic: Thieves have roots and accomplices; I ask that the Prince of Yi's household members and the banner bondservant be arrested and thoroughly investigated."

sentences.zh: 上下其疏，罪人皆抵法。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down through the offices, and all the guilty were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was circulated for action, and all the guilty were punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 國初考功法，獲逃人、闢荒田、督運漕糧，皆躐等升擢。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty the merit-assessment regulations provided that capturing fugitives, opening wasteland, and supervising transport of tribute grain all led to promotion by skipped grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the early dynasty's merit-assessment system, capturing fugitives, opening wasteland, and supervising tribute-grain transport all earned promotion by skipped grades.

sentences.zh: 希轍疏爭非政體，不當開幸進。

translations.literal: Xizhe memorialized in opposition that this was not sound governmental practice and ought not to open a path of favor-seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe memorialized in protest that this was not sound governance and ought not to open a door to advancement by favor.

sentences.zh: 上方嚴罪貪吏，吏往往曲法罰鍰。

translations.literal: The emperor was then imposing severe penalties on corrupt officials, and officials often bent the law to impose fines in money.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then imposing severe penalties on corrupt officials, and officials often bent the law to levy fines in cash.

sentences.zh: 希轍疏言：「例贖杖分有力無力，所輕重不過銖兩間。

translations.literal: Xizhe memorialized: "The statutes on commutation of the bastinado distinguish the able from the unable; the difference in severity amounts to no more than a few cash.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe memorialized: "The statutes on commuting the bastinado distinguish those able to pay from those unable; the difference in severity amounts to no more than a few cash.

sentences.zh: 今乃倍五倍十，不拘成數，不應則敲樸隨之。

translations.literal: Now it is multiplied fivefold or tenfold, without regard to the fixed amounts, and if one does not comply the cudgel follows immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Now fines are multiplied five- or tenfold without regard to the fixed amounts, and if one does not comply the cudgel follows at once.

sentences.zh: 是昔以罰省刑，今以罰濟刑也。」

translations.literal: In the past fines were used to reduce corporal punishment; now fines are used to supply corporal punishment."
translations.idiomatic: In the past fines were meant to spare the body; now fines are used to supply corporal punishment."

sentences.zh: 命仍如定例。

translations.literal: An order was issued to adhere again to the established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered that the established regulations be followed again.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上詔求言，希轍疏言：「臣聞君臣一德，原未嘗以憂勞之任獨歸之君父，為人臣諉卸責地也。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor issued an edict seeking counsel; Xizhe memorialized: "Your subject has heard that ruler and minister share one virtue, and it was never originally intended that the burden of anxious toil should rest solely on the sovereign and father, leaving subjects a place to shirk responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor issued an edict soliciting counsel; Xizhe memorialized: "I have heard that ruler and minister share one virtue, and it was never meant that the burden of anxious toil should rest solely on the sovereign, leaving ministers room to shirk their duty.

sentences.zh: 臣觀今日積習病根，大要有二：巧於卸肩者，假詳慎以行推諉；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that the deep-rooted habits of the present day fall chiefly into two categories: those skilled at shifting burdens feign meticulous caution in order to practice evasion;
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the deep-rooted habits of the day fall chiefly into two kinds: those skilled at shifting burdens feign meticulous caution in order to evade responsibility;

sentences.zh: 畏於任事者，飾持重以蹈委靡。

translations.literal: those who fear taking on affairs adorn themselves with weighty reserve and fall into slackness.
translations.idiomatic: those who fear taking on affairs cloak themselves in weighty reserve and sink into slackness.

sentences.zh: 請進一德之箴，為中外諸臣誡。」

translations.literal: I beg that a maxim on shared virtue be advanced as a warning to all officials within and without the capital."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a maxim on shared virtue be offered as a warning to all officials at court and in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 師自江西下廣東，州縣供億繁重。

translations.literal: As the army advanced from Jiangxi into Guangdong, the burden of provisioning on prefectures and counties was heavy.
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced from Jiangxi into Guangdong, the burden of provisioning on prefectures and counties grew crushing.

sentences.zh: 南贛巡撫報曲江、始興兩知縣同時自戕。

translations.literal: The governor of southern Gan reported that the magistrates of Qujiang and Shixing had killed themselves at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of southern Gan reported that the magistrates of Qujiang and Shixing had taken their own lives on the same day.

sentences.zh: 希轍疏言：「大兵所集，米豆、草束、槽秬、釜鑊，自所必需。

translations.literal: Xizhe memorialized: "Where great armies gather, grain, beans, bundles of fodder, troughs, grain measures, and cooking pots are naturally indispensable.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe memorialized: "Where great armies gather, grain, beans, fodder bundles, troughs, grain measures, and cooking pots are naturally indispensable.

sentences.zh: 然先時傳檄，使之預備，供億雖艱，何至捐僨？

translations.literal: Yet if proclamations are sent in advance so that preparations may be made, though provisioning is arduous, how could it come to men perishing?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if orders are sent in advance so that preparations can be made, however arduous provisioning may be, how could it drive men to throw away their lives?

sentences.zh: 行兵不嚴，責在總督；

translations.literal: If troop movements are not disciplined, the responsibility lies with the governor-general;
translations.idiomatic: If troop movements are not disciplined, the governor-general is responsible;

sentences.zh: 立法不預，責在巡撫：二者必居一於是。

translations.literal: if regulations are not made in advance, the responsibility lies with the provincial governor: one of the two must apply here.
translations.idiomatic: if regulations are not laid down in advance, the provincial governor is responsible: one of the two must be at fault.

sentences.zh: 請飭察究。」

translations.literal: I beg that this be ordered investigated."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be ordered investigated."

sentences.zh: 尋更歷兵、禮二科。

translations.literal: He soon served in succession in the Military and Rites sections.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served in succession in the Military and Rites sections of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時會計法嚴，錢糧完欠，每項各限十分定考成，條例繁賾，有司救過不給。

translations.literal: At the time the accounting regulations were strict; for each item of revenue and grain collected or outstanding a ten-part scale fixed the merit assessment, the statutes were numerous and cumbersome, and local officials could not keep up with remedying their errors.
translations.idiomatic: At the time accounting rules were strict: for each revenue item collected or outstanding, a ten-part scale fixed merit assessment; the regulations were numerous and cumbersome, and local officials could not keep pace with correcting their errors.

sentences.zh: 希轍疏請：「總歸十分，以一歲之徵收，計一歲之款項，起訖既清，稽核亦便。」

translations.literal: Xizhe memorialized requesting: "Let everything be summed to ten parts, calculating one year's receipts against one year's accounts; once beginning and end are clear, audit is also convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe memorialized requesting: "Let everything be summed to ten parts, matching one year's collections against one year's accounts; once the period is clear, audit is straightforward as well."

sentences.zh: 自此部計稍紓，有司得久任。

translations.literal: From this the ministry's accounting was somewhat eased, and local officials were able to serve longer terms.
translations.idiomatic: From this ministry accounting was somewhat eased, and local officials were able to serve longer terms.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，考滿，內升，回籍待缺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, when his term assessment was complete, he was promoted within the capital ranks and returned to his native place to await appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi, when his term assessment was complete, he was promoted within the capital ranks and returned home to await appointment.

sentences.zh: 九年，詣京師，复授戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went to the capital and was again appointed chief supervising secretary of the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he went to the capital and was again appointed chief supervising secretary of the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 具三疏：請增科員；

translations.literal: He submitted three memorials: requesting an increase in the number of section members;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials: to increase the number of censorial section members;

sentences.zh: 請令巡撫得轄兵，防地方竊發；

translations.literal: requesting that provincial governors be allowed to command troops to guard against local outbreaks;
translations.idiomatic: to allow provincial governors to command troops against local outbreaks;

sentences.zh: 請緩奏銷之期，使催科不迫。

translations.literal: requesting that the deadline for submitting final accounts be relaxed so that tax collection would not be pressed.
translations.idiomatic: and to relax the deadline for final accounts so that tax collection would not be pressed so hard.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪歸。

translations.literal: When his father died he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授奉天府丞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乞養母歸。

translations.literal: He begged leave to return home and support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to return home and care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 餘縉，字仲紳，浙江諸暨人。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, style name Zhongshen, was a native of Zhuji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, whose style was Zhongshen, came from Zhuji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授河南封丘知縣。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of Fengqiu in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of Fengqiu in Henan.

sentences.zh: 兵後流亡未復，棄地彌望，朝議興屯，設道、廳董之。

translations.literal: After the wars the displaced had not returned, and abandoned fields stretched as far as one could see; the court discussed opening military colonies and established circuit and bureau offices to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars the displaced had not returned, and abandoned fields stretched to the horizon; the court discussed opening military colonies and set up circuit and bureau offices to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 民田徵賦，屯田徵租，租視賦為重，民棄屯不耕。

translations.literal: Private fields were taxed by land tax, colony fields by rent, and rent was heavier than tax, so the people abandoned the colonies and did not cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: Private fields paid land tax while colony fields paid rent, and rent was heavier than tax, so people abandoned the colonies and left them uncultivated.

sentences.zh: 府縣吏急考成，以屯租散入田賦，民失業。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county clerks, anxious about merit assessment, spread colony rent into land tax, and the people lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county clerks, anxious about merit assessment, folded colony rent into land tax, and the people lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 總督李廕祖行部至縣，縉導觀民間困苦狀，廕祖疏聞，興屯道、廳悉罷。

translations.literal: When Governor-General Li Yinzu made an inspection tour to the county, Jin led him to observe the people's distress; Yinzu memorialized the throne, and all the colony circuit and bureau offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Li Yinzu toured the county, Jin led him to see the people's distress; Yinzu memorialized the throne, and all the colony circuit and bureau offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十七年，行取授山西道御史，乞養歸。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, selected for promotion, he was appointed censor of the Shanxi circuit and begged leave to return home and support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, selected for promotion, he was appointed censor of the Shanxi circuit and begged leave to return home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 起河南道御史。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as censor of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as censor of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，鄭成功已死，其子錦屯廈門。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, Zheng Chenggong was already dead, and his son Jing was encamped at Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, Zheng Chenggong was already dead, and his son Jing held Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 有議棄舟山者，縉上疏爭之，略謂：「浙江三面環海，寧波尤孤懸海隅，以舟山為外籓。

translations.literal: When some proposed abandoning Zhoushan, Jin memorialized in opposition, stating in part: "Zhejiang is surrounded by sea on three sides, and Ningbo especially stands isolated on the coast, with Zhoushan as its outer bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed abandoning Zhoushan, Jin memorialized in opposition, arguing in part: "Zhejiang is ringed by sea on three sides, and Ningbo especially stands isolated on the coast, with Zhoushan as its outer bulwark.

sentences.zh: 不知行間諸臣何所見而倡捐棄之議？

translations.literal: I do not know what those officials in the field have seen to advocate a proposal to surrender and abandon it?
translations.idiomatic: What have the officials in the field seen to advocate surrendering it?

sentences.zh: 江海門戶，斂手委之逆豎。

translations.literal: The gateway of river and sea—are we to fold our hands and hand it over to rebellious upstarts?
translations.idiomatic: The gateway of river and sea—are we to fold our hands and hand it to rebellious upstarts?

sentences.zh: 夫閩海祗一廈門，數万之眾，環而攻之，窮年不能下。

translations.literal: In Fujian's seas there is only Xiamen; tens of thousands surround and attack it, yet for a full year they cannot take it.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian's seas there is only Xiamen; tens of thousands besiege it, yet a full year cannot bring it down.

sentences.zh: 奈何以已克之舟山增其巢穴？」

translations.literal: How can we add to their lair a Zhoushan already taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Why would we hand them Zhoushan, which we have already taken, to enlarge their lair?"

sentences.zh: 福建總督李率泰議遷海濱居民，縉复疏爭之。

translations.literal: Fujian Governor-General Li Shuaitai proposed relocating coastal inhabitants, and Jin again memorialized in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Governor-General Li Shuaitai proposed relocating coastal inhabitants, and Jin again memorialized in opposition.

sentences.zh: 略謂：「海濱之民，與賊狎處。

translations.literal: He stated in part: "The people of the coast live in familiar proximity with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He argued in part: "Coastal people live in familiar proximity with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 一二冥頑貪狡，嗜厚利，通消息，以相接濟者，固未必無之。

translations.literal: One or two obstinate and greedy men who crave great profit, pass messages, and supply mutual aid—such cases are certainly not impossible.
translations.idiomatic: A few obstinate and greedy men who crave great profit, pass messages, and supply mutual aid—such cases certainly exist.

sentences.zh: 但據所稱排頭、方田諸處，民或盜牧馬，或縛窮民潛送廈門。

translations.literal: But according to what is alleged at Paitou, Fangtian, and other places, the people either steal pastured horses or bind poor men and secretly send them to Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: But according to what is alleged at Paitou, Fangtian, and other places, locals either steal pastured horses or bind poor men and secretly send them to Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 當此兩軍相望，​​巡徼嚴密，雖有姦宄，安能飛渡？

translations.literal: At a time when the two armies face each other and patrols are strict, even if there are traitors, how could they fly across?
translations.idiomatic: With the two armies facing each other and patrols strict, even if traitors exist, how could they cross unseen?

sentences.zh: 是其號令不肅，已可概見。」

translations.literal: That their orders are not disciplined can already be seen in broad outline."
translations.idiomatic: That their discipline is lax can already be seen plainly."

sentences.zh: 又云：「派撥舵工、水手，公然不應。

translations.literal: He also said: "When helmsmen and sailors are assigned by levy, they openly refuse to comply.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "When helmsmen and sailors are assigned by levy, they openly refuse to comply.

sentences.zh: 海上舵工名曰「老大」，其人必少長海舟內，外洋島嶼徑路，靡不熟歷，而後駕風使舵，操縱自如。

translations.literal: Sea helmsmen are called laoda; such a man must have grown up from youth aboard seagoing vessels and know every route among outer islands without exception, and only then can he ride the wind and work the rudder with free command.
translations.idiomatic: Sea helmsmen are called laoda; such men must have grown up aboard seagoing vessels and know every route among outer islands by heart before they can ride the wind, work the rudder, and handle a ship with ease.

sentences.zh: 奈何責之素不練習之民，視同里役，橫加僉派？

translations.literal: How can one demand this of people who have never practiced it, treat them like corvée labor within the li, and impose assignment by force?
translations.idiomatic: How can one demand this of people who have never practiced it, treat them like neighborhood corvée labor, and impose forced assignment?

sentences.zh: 彼即勉強應役，技既不精，心复叵測。

translations.literal: Even if they force themselves to serve, their skill is not refined and their hearts are moreover hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they force themselves to serve, their skill is crude and their intentions impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 萬一變從中起，將置數十萬奮戈持滿之士於何地？」

translations.literal: If by chance a mutiny arises from within, where will hundreds of thousands of men brandishing weapons and drawing bows be placed?"
translations.idiomatic: If a mutiny breaks out among them, where will hundreds of thousands of armed troops be left?"

sentences.zh: 兩疏語皆切至。

translations.literal: The language of both memorials was penetrating and to the point.
translations.idiomatic: The language of both memorials was penetrating and to the point.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，順治間建言諸臣坐遷謫者，次第赦還，惟議及逃人不在赦例。

translations.literal: When the Sage Emperor took personal rule, the officials who had been banished during Shunzhi for offering counsel were pardoned and recalled in succession, except that those who had spoken on fugitive slaves were not within the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sage Emperor took personal rule, officials banished during Shunzhi for offering counsel were pardoned and recalled in turn, except those who had spoken on fugitive slaves, who were not covered by the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 居數年，詔寬逃人禁。

translations.literal: After several years an edict relaxed the prohibition on fugitive slaves.
translations.idiomatic: After several years an edict relaxed the prohibition on fugitive slaves.

sentences.zh: 縉疏請敕部察當日建言被謫諸臣，存者召還錄用，歿者歸葬贈卹。

translations.literal: Jin memorialized requesting that the ministry be ordered to investigate the officials banished in those days for offering counsel: those still living should be recalled and employed, those deceased should be given burial at home and posthumous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Jin memorialized asking that the ministry investigate the officials banished in those days for offering counsel: survivors should be recalled and employed, the dead given burial at home and posthumous rewards.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視長蘆鹽政。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to inspect the Changlu salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to inspect the Changlu salt administration.

sentences.zh: 以改葬乞歸。

translations.literal: He begged leave to return home for a reburial.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to return home for a reburial.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 縉廉而能，治事尤持正。

translations.literal: Jin was incorruptible and capable, and especially upright in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was incorruptible and capable, and especially upright in handling affairs.

sentences.zh: 妖人硃方旦言禍福，朝士多信之。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Zhu Fangdan spoke of fortune and misfortune, and many court officials believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Zhu Fangdan spoke of fortune and misfortune, and many court officials believed him.

sentences.zh: 縉曰：「此妄男子耳，於法當誅。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "This is merely a deluded man; by law he ought to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said: "He is merely a deluded man; by law he ought to be executed."

sentences.zh: 方旦卒坐死。

translations.literal: Fangdan ultimately died by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Fangdan was ultimately executed.

sentences.zh: 德格勒，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Degele was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Degele was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the ninth year of Kangxi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Kangxi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累擢侍讀學士，充日講起居注官、掌院學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to reader-in-waiting, served as daily lecturer and recorder of the emperor's movements and residences, and became chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to reader-in-waiting, served as daily lecturer and recorder of the emperor's movements and residences, and became chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 李光地亟稱其賢。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi repeatedly praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi repeatedly praised his worth.

sentences.zh: 聖祖時，召見講論經史，嘗扈從巡行。

translations.literal: In the time of the Sage Emperor he was summoned to audience to discuss the classics and histories, and once accompanied the emperor on tour.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sage Emperor he was summoned to discuss the classics and histories and once accompanied the emperor on tour.

sentences.zh: 大學士明珠柄政，務結納士大夫，將餽金為治裝。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Mingzhu held power and strove to win over scholar-officials; he was about to present gold as travel funds.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Mingzhu held power and worked to win over scholar-officials; he was about to present gold as travel funds.

sentences.zh: 德格勒以裝具，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Degele, on the grounds that he already had his outfit, firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Degele, saying he already had his outfit, firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 會久旱，上命德格勒筮，遇夬。

translations.literal: When a long drought occurred, the emperor ordered Degele to divine by the Changes and he obtained Guai.
translations.idiomatic: During a long drought the emperor ordered Degele to divine by the Changes; he obtained Guai.

sentences.zh: 問其占，曰：「澤上於天，將降矣！

translations.literal: Asked about the omen, he said: "The marsh is above heaven—rain is about to fall!
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the omen, he said: "The marsh is above heaven—rain is about to fall!

sentences.zh: 而卦義五陽決一陰。

translations.literal: Yet the meaning of the hexagram is that five yang lines decide one yin line.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the hexagram's meaning is that five yang lines decide one yin.

sentences.zh: 小人居鼎鉉，故天屯其膏。

translations.literal: Petty men occupy the tripod and the cauldron, and therefore Heaven hoards its bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men hold high office, and so Heaven hoards its bounty.

sentences.zh: 決去之，即雨。」

translations.literal: Remove them decisively, and rain will come at once."
translations.idiomatic: Remove them decisively, and rain will come at once."

sentences.zh: 上愕然，曰：「安有是？」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said: "How can that be?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and said, "How can that be?"

sentences.zh: 德格勒遂以明珠對。

translations.literal: Degele then named Mingzhu in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Degele then named Mingzhu in reply.

sentences.zh: 明珠聞，大惡之，時以蜚語上聞，謂德格勒與侍講徐元夢互相標榜。

translations.literal: When Mingzhu heard this he hated him greatly; from time to time slander reached the emperor's ears, saying that Degele and the lecturer Xu Yuanmeng were mutually promoting each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzhu heard this he hated him deeply; from time to time slander reached the emperor, claiming that Degele and lecturer Xu Yuanmeng were promoting each other.

sentences.zh: 徐元夢亦不附明珠者也，故並嫉之。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanmeng also did not attach himself to Mingzhu, and therefore both were envied together.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanmeng also refused to attach himself to Mingzhu, and so Mingzhu envied them both.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，光地乞假歸，入辭，面奏德格勒、徐元夢學博文優。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Guangdi begged leave to return home; on taking leave in audience he reported in person that Degele and Xu Yuanmeng were learned, broadly cultured, and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Li Guangdi begged leave to return home; on taking leave in audience he reported that Degele and Xu Yuanmeng were learned, broadly cultured, and excellent.

sentences.zh: 踰月，上召尚書陳廷敬、湯斌等及德格勒、徐元夢試於乾清宮。

translations.literal: After more than a month the emperor summoned the ministers Chen Tingjing, Tang Bin, and others, together with Degele and Xu Yuanmeng, to be examined in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the emperor summoned Ministers Chen Tingjing, Tang Bin, and others, together with Degele and Xu Yuanmeng, to an examination in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 閱卷畢，諭曰：「朕政暇好讀書，然不輕評論古人。

translations.literal: When the papers had been reviewed, he instructed: "In my spare time from government I love to read books, yet I do not lightly comment on men of old.
translations.idiomatic: When the papers had been reviewed, he said: "In my spare time from government I love to read, yet I do not lightly judge men of old.

sentences.zh: 評論古人猶易，評論時人更難。

translations.literal: To comment on men of old is still easy; to comment on men of the present is harder still.
translations.idiomatic: Judging men of old is still easy; judging men of the present is harder still.

sentences.zh: 如德格勒每評論時人，朕心不謂然，故召爾等面試。

translations.literal: As when Degele constantly comments on men of the present—my heart does not agree—therefore I have summoned you for a face-to-face examination.
translations.idiomatic: Degele constantly comments on men of the present, and I do not agree; that is why I have summoned you for a face-to-face examination.

sentences.zh: 妍媸優劣，今已判然。

translations.literal: Beauty and ugliness, excellence and inferiority, are now clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Excellence and inferiority are now clearly distinguished.

sentences.zh: 學問自有分量，毋徒肆議論為也。」

translations.literal: Learning has its own weight; do not merely indulge in loose discussion."
translations.idiomatic: Learning has its own weight; do not indulge in loose talk alone."

sentences.zh: 二十七年，明珠罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Mingzhu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Mingzhu was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，掌院學士庫勒訥劾德格勒私抹起居注，並與徐元夢互相標榜，下刑部論罪。

translations.literal: Before long, Hanlin chancellor Kullene impeached Degele for privately altering the court diaries and for mutually promoting each other with Xu Yuanmeng; the case was sent to the Ministry of Punishments to determine guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Hanlin chancellor Kullene impeached Degele for privately altering the court diaries and for promoting each other with Xu Yuanmeng; the case was sent to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 故事，起居注數易藁然後登籍，德格勒所刪易者，實未定藁也。

translations.literal: By precedent the court diaries were revised through many drafts before being entered in the register; what Degele had deleted and altered were in fact not yet finalized drafts.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the court diaries went through many drafts before registration; what Degele had altered were not yet finalized drafts.

sentences.zh: 讞上論斬，命改​​監候秋後處決，徐元夢亦坐譴。

translations.literal: When the verdict was submitted it called for decapitation; an order changed this to imprisonment awaiting autumn execution, and Xu Yuanmeng was also punished by reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict called for decapitation; an order changed this to imprisonment awaiting autumn execution, and Xu Yuanmeng was also reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 語詳徐元夢傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Xu Yuanmeng.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Xu Yuanmeng.

sentences.zh: 光地還京師，上命尚書張玉書等以德格勒試卷示九卿，並詰光地。

translations.literal: When Guangdi returned to the capital, the emperor ordered Minister Zhang Yushu and others to show Degele's examination papers to the Nine Ministers and also to question Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangdi returned to the capital, the emperor ordered Minister Zhang Yushu and others to show Degele's examination papers to the Nine Ministers and to question Guangdi as well.

sentences.zh: 於是玉書等奏稱德格勒文實鄙陋，光地亦以妄奏引罪，命從寬免究。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yushu and the others memorialized that Degele's writing was in fact crude and vulgar; Guangdi also took blame for his false report, and an order was issued to pardon them leniently without further investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yushu and the others memorialized that Degele's writing was crude and vulgar; Guangdi also took blame for his false report, and both were leniently pardoned.

sentences.zh: 德格勒尋遇赦，釋歸本旗。

translations.literal: Degele soon encountered an amnesty, was released, and returned to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Degele was soon amnestied, released, and returned to his banner.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 陳紫芝，字非園，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Zizhi, style name Feiyuan, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zizhi, whose style was Feiyuan, came from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the eighteenth year of Kangxi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Kangxi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 改陝西道御史，力持風紀，絕外僚餽遺。

translations.literal: Transferred to censor of the Shaanxi circuit, he vigorously upheld discipline and cut off gifts from outside officials.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to censor of the Shaanxi circuit, he vigorously upheld discipline and refused gifts from outside officials.

sentences.zh: 巡視南城，捕大猾鄧二置諸法。

translations.literal: While inspecting the southern city he captured the great rogue Deng Er and punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the southern city he captured the notorious rogue Deng Er and punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「朝章國典宜畫一，民間冠昏喪祭未有定制，請編纂禮書，頒行天下。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Court regulations and state statutes ought to be uniform; among the people there is as yet no fixed standard for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice—please compile a book of rites and promulgate it throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Court regulations and state statutes ought to be uniform; the people still lack fixed standards for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice—please compile a book of rites and promulgate it throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 又請裁屯衛：「以屯務屬州縣，則田賦可覈，逃盜可清。」

translations.literal: He also requested the abolition of garrison colonies: "If colony affairs are placed under prefectures and counties, then land tax can be audited and fugitives and bandits cleared away."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to abolish garrison colonies: "If colony affairs were placed under prefectures and counties, land tax could be audited and fugitives and bandits cleared away."

sentences.zh: 詔並允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved both requests for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 時督、撫、監司皆由廷臣保舉。

translations.literal: At the time governors-general, governors, and surveillance commissioners were all recommended by court officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the time governors-general, governors, and surveillance commissioners were all recommended by court officials.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡撫張汧，大學士明珠所私也，恃勢貪暴，言路莫敢摘發。

translations.literal: Huguang Governor Zhang Qian was a protégé of Grand Secretary Mingzhu; relying on his power he was greedy and violent, and no one on the remonstrance track dared expose him.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Governor Zhang Qian was a protégé of Grand Secretary Mingzhu; relying on his power he was greedy and violent, and no censor dared expose him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，紫芝上疏劾之，言：「汧蒞任未久，黷貨多端，凡地方鹽引、錢局、船埠，靡不搜括，甚至漢口市肆招牌，亦按數派錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Zizhi memorialized to impeach him, stating: "Qian has not long held his post, yet his corrupt taking of goods has many forms; every local salt franchise, money bureau, and ferry landing he extorts without exception, even to the point of levying money by count on shop signs in Hankou market.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Zizhi memorialized to impeach him, stating: "Qian has not long held his post, yet he is corrupt in many ways; he extorts every local salt franchise, money bureau, and ferry landing, even levying money by count on shop signs in Hankou market.

sentences.zh: 當日保舉之人，必有賄囑情弊，請一併敕部論罪。」

translations.literal: Those who recommended him at the time must certainly have been involved in bribery and collusion—please order the ministry to punish them all together."
translations.idiomatic: Those who recommended him must have been involved in bribery—please order the ministry to punish them as well."

sentences.zh: 上命奪汧官，遣直隸巡撫於成龍、山西巡撫馬齊、副都御史開音布往按治。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Qian stripped of office and dispatched Zhili Governor Yu Chenglong, Shanxi Governor Ma Qi, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Kai Yinbu to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Qian of office and dispatched Zhili Governor Yu Chenglong, Shanxi Governor Ma Qi, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Kai Yinbu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 复諭廷臣，謂汧貪婪無人敢言，紫芝獨能彈劾，即予內升。

translations.literal: He again instructed the court officials, saying that Qian was greedy yet no one dared speak, while Zizhi alone was able to impeach him, and immediately granted him promotion within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He again told the court that Qian was greedy yet no one dared speak, while Zizhi alone impeached him, and immediately granted him promotion within the capital.

sentences.zh: 成龍等按得汧以前官福建布政使虧帑令屬吏彌補，又派收鹽商銀九萬，上荊南道祖澤深婪取於民又八萬，讞上，論絞。

translations.literal: Chenglong and the others investigated and found that when Qian had previously served as Fujian provincial treasurer he had a deficit in the treasury made up by subordinate clerks, and also forcibly collected ninety thousand taels from salt merchants; his superior, Jingnan Circuit Intendant Zu Zeshen, had greedily taken another eighty thousand from the people; when the verdict was submitted the sentence was strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong and the others found that as Fujian provincial treasurer Qian had covered treasury deficits through subordinates and forcibly collected ninety thousand taels from salt merchants; his superior Zu Zeshen had greedily taken another eighty thousand from the people; the verdict called for strangulation.

sentences.zh: 保舉汧為巡撫者，侍郎王遵訓、學士盧琦、大理寺丞任辰旦，皆坐奪官。

translations.literal: Those who had recommended Qian as governor—Vice Minister Wang Zunxun, Academician Lu Qi, and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Ren Chendan—were all punished by loss of office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zunxun, Lu Qi, and Ren Chendan, who had recommended Qian as governor, were all stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 擢紫芝大理少卿。

translations.literal: Zizhi was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 每讞獄，稍涉矜疑，即為駁正，多所平反。

translations.literal: Whenever he reviewed cases, if there was the slightest ground for compassionate doubt he would overturn the verdict, and many were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he reviewed cases, if there was the slightest ground for doubt he overturned the verdict, and many were reversed.

sentences.zh: 紫芝以峭直受上知，同朝多側目。

translations.literal: Zizhi, through his stern uprightness, won the emperor's trust, and many colleagues in court looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi won the emperor's trust through his stern uprightness, and many colleagues looked askance at him.

sentences.zh: 無何，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 或傳紫芝一日詣朝房，明珠延坐進茗，飲之，歸遂暴卒雲。

translations.literal: Some spread the rumor that one day Zizhi went to the morning assembly hall, Mingzhu invited him to sit and served tea, he drank it, and on returning suddenly died—or so it was said.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that one day Zizhi went to the morning assembly hall, Mingzhu invited him to sit and served tea, he drank it, and died suddenly on returning home.

sentences.zh: 笪重光，字在辛，江南句容人。

translations.literal: Da Chongguang, style name Zaixin, was a native of Jurong in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Da Chongguang, whose style was Zaixin, came from Jurong in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the ninth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 自刑部郎中考選御史。

translations.literal: From a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments he was selected by examination as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: From a post in the Ministry of Punishments he was selected by examination as a censor.

sentences.zh: 巡按江西，與明珠忤，罷歸。

translations.literal: While touring and inspecting Jiangxi he clashed with Mingzhu and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Jiangxi he clashed with Mingzhu and was dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭成功犯鎮江，重光縋城乞援。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zheng Chenggong attacked Zhenjiang, Chongguang let himself down from the city wall by rope to beg for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zheng Chenggong attacked Zhenjiang, Chongguang let himself down from the wall by rope to beg for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 事平，賜御書榜。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was granted an imperial inscription plaque.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled he was granted an imperial inscription plaque.

sentences.zh: 卒，祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: He died and was enshrined among the local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was enshrined among the local worthies.

sentences.zh: 任弘嘉，字葵尊，江南宜興人。

translations.literal: Ren Hongjia, style name Kuizun, was a native of Yixing in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Hongjia, whose style was Kuizun, came from Yixing in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 初以舉人官行人。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate, he served as a courier official.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as a provincial graduate, he served as a courier official.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 十八年，考選江南道御史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, selected by examination, he became censor of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was selected by examination as censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡南城，疏言：「各州縣宜有講堂書院，庶人知鄉學。」

translations.literal: While inspecting the southern city he memorialized: "Every prefecture and county ought to have lecture halls and academies so that the common people may know village learning."
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the southern city he memorialized: "Every prefecture and county ought to have lecture halls and academies so the common people may know village learning."

sentences.zh: 又言：「學道不惟受制籓司，抑且受制知府。

translations.literal: He also said: "The educational commissioner is not only constrained by the provincial administration commissioner but is further constrained by the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The educational commissioner is constrained not only by the provincial administration commissioner but by the prefect as well.

sentences.zh: 蓋府道階級不甚懸，無以資表率。

translations.literal: For the ranks of prefecture and circuit are not greatly separated, and there is no basis for setting an example.
translations.idiomatic: For prefectural and circuit ranks are not greatly separated, leaving no basis for setting an example.

sentences.zh: 部郎聲望不甚重，又無由達封章。

translations.literal: A ministry director's prestige is not very weighty, and moreover there is no channel for sealed memorials to reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: A ministry director's prestige is not weighty enough, and there is no channel for sealed memorials to reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 求其公明，實不可得，乞重其選。」

translations.literal: To seek fairness and clarity from such a post is in fact unattainable; I beg that greater weight be given to its selection."
translations.idiomatic: Fairness and clarity from such a post are unattainable; I ask that greater weight be given to its selection."

sentences.zh: 改巡北城，疏陳五城應行事，謂：「盜風未靖，由保甲不行。

translations.literal: Transferred to inspect the northern city, he memorialized on what the Five Wards ought to undertake, stating: "Banditry is not yet pacified because the baojia system is not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to inspect the northern city, he memorialized on what the Five Wards ought to do, stating: "Banditry is not yet pacified because the baojia system is not enforced.

sentences.zh: 稽察未清，由旗、民雜處。

translations.literal: Inspection is not clear because banner people and civilians are mixed together.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection is unclear because banner people and civilians are mixed together.

sentences.zh: 司坊未潔，由勸懲不當。」

translations.literal: Ward administration is not clean because encouragement and punishment are not applied properly."
translations.idiomatic: Ward administration is not clean because encouragement and punishment are misapplied."

sentences.zh: 又言：「州縣昏夜比較，鄉民託宿無地，飢寒受杖，往往殞命。

translations.literal: He also said: "When prefectures and counties conduct night-time tax comparisons, village people have nowhere to lodge; starving and cold they are beaten with the staff and often lose their lives.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When prefectures and counties conduct night-time tax comparisons, villagers have nowhere to lodge; starving and cold they are beaten and often die.

sentences.zh: 又或因分釐火耗之輕，受僉役橫索之累。」

translations.literal: Or again because the surcharge for melting loss is slight, they suffer the burden of forced exactions by levy clerks."
translations.idiomatic: Or again because the melting-loss surcharge is slight, they suffer forced exactions by levy clerks."

sentences.zh: 又言：「朝廷清丈，所以為民，而籓府駁冊，上下動費累百。

translations.literal: He also said: "The court's land surveys are meant to benefit the people, yet when princely establishments reject the registers, above and below each case costs hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The court's land surveys are meant to benefit the people, yet when princely establishments reject the registers, each case costs hundreds above and below.

sentences.zh: 津梁有關，所以御暴，今小港皆設巡攔，旱路亦行堵截，檢索至負擔，稅課遍雞豚。」

translations.literal: Ferry crossings and bridges have barriers to control violence; now small harbors all set up patrol posts, overland routes also conduct stop-and-search, inspection extends even to porters' loads, and taxes reach even to chickens and pigs."
translations.idiomatic: Ferry crossings and bridges have barriers to control violence; now small harbors all have patrol posts, overland routes conduct stop-and-search, inspection extends to porters' loads, and taxes reach even chickens and pigs."

sentences.zh: 所言皆痛切。

translations.literal: Everything he said was piercing and to the point.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he said was piercing and to the point.

sentences.zh: 弘嘉一日巡城，有錦衣駿馬突其前，訶叱之。

translations.literal: One day while Hongjia was patrolling the city, a man in brocade on a fine horse rushed before him, and he shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: One day while Hongjia was patrolling the city, a man in brocade on a fine horse rushed before him, and he shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 隸卒白曰：「此王府優也。」

translations.literal: A runner reported: "This is an actor of the princely establishment."
translations.idiomatic: A runner said, "This is an actor from the princely establishment."

sentences.zh: 弘嘉趨王府，索優出，杖之四十。

translations.literal: Hongjia hurried to the princely residence, demanded that the actor be produced, and had him beaten forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjia went straight to the princely residence, demanded the actor be produced, and had him beaten forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 上聞，直弘嘉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he upheld Hongjia.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he upheld Hongjia.

sentences.zh: 由是貴戚斂跡，毋敢玩法。

translations.literal: From this the noble kin restrained themselves and did not dare to trifle with the law.
translations.idiomatic: From this the noble kin restrained themselves and did not dare trifle with the law.

sentences.zh: 尋掌山東道，兼江南道如故。

translations.literal: Soon he took charge of the Shandong circuit while continuing to hold the Jiangnan circuit as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took charge of the Shandong circuit while continuing to hold the Jiangnan circuit as before.

sentences.zh: 上十漸疏：「一曰，朋黨交結之漸。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on ten gradual deteriorations: "First, the gradual growth of factional cliques and mutual entanglement.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on ten gradual deteriorations: "First, the gradual growth of factional cliques and mutual entanglement.

sentences.zh: 始因交際為餽遺，漸以愛憎成水火。

translations.literal: It begins with social intercourse and gift-giving, and gradually love and hatred become fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: It begins with social intercourse and gift-giving, and gradually love and hatred become irreconcilable.

sentences.zh: 二曰，奢侈僭逾之漸。

translations.literal: Second, the gradual growth of extravagance and presumptuous excess.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the gradual growth of extravagance and presumptuous excess.

sentences.zh: 物力既殫，等威亦紊。

translations.literal: Material resources are exhausted, and ranks of dignity are also disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Material resources are exhausted, and ranks of dignity are disordered as well.

sentences.zh: 三曰，文武訐訕之漸。

translations.literal: Third, the gradual growth of mutual denunciation between civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the gradual growth of mutual denunciation between civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、提、鎮挾私互訐，小吏效尤，何以使民無訟？

translations.literal: Governors-general, governors, provincial military commanders, and regional commanders denounce one another with private motives; petty clerks follow suit—how can the people be kept free of litigation?
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general, governors, provincial military commanders, and regional commanders denounce one another with private motives; petty clerks follow suit—how can the people be kept free of litigation?

sentences.zh: 四曰，紳士吹求之漸。

translations.literal: Fourth, the gradual growth of gentry pressing demands.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the gradual growth of gentry pressing demands.

sentences.zh: 有司視如仇讎，奸民以為魚肉。

translations.literal: Local officials regard them as mortal enemies, while scoundrels treat the people as meat on the chopping block.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials regard them as enemies, while scoundrels treat the people as prey.

sentences.zh: 五曰，上下奉違之漸。

translations.literal: Fifth, the gradual growth of contradiction between higher and lower levels in carrying out orders.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the gradual growth of contradiction between higher and lower levels in carrying out orders.

sentences.zh: 國家良法美意，奉行者徒有虛文，過當者反成弊政。

translations.literal: The state's good laws and fine intentions are carried out only as empty forms by those who implement them, while those who go too far turn them into harmful policies.
translations.idiomatic: The state's good laws and fine intentions are carried out only as empty forms, while those who go too far turn them into harmful policies.

sentences.zh: 六曰，名器混淆之漸。

translations.literal: Sixth, the gradual confusion of titles and offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the gradual confusion of titles and offices.

sentences.zh: 為生養萬民計，守令宜用正途。

translations.literal: For the sake of nurturing the myriad people, prefects and magistrates ought to be appointed through the regular path.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of nurturing the people, prefects and magistrates ought to be appointed through the regular path.

sentences.zh: 七曰，常平侵漁之漸。

translations.literal: Seventh, the gradual encroachment and exploitation of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the gradual encroachment and exploitation of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 貯穀久易浥損，又難盤察，不若聽民輸錢，數易稽而無朽蠹。

translations.literal: Stored grain over time easily becomes damp and spoiled, and is also hard to audit; it would be better to let the people pay in money, which is easy to count and free of rot and worms.
translations.idiomatic: Stored grain easily spoils over time and is hard to audit; it would be better to let people pay in money, which is easy to count and free of rot and worms.

sentences.zh: 八曰，河工興建之漸。

translations.literal: Eighth, the gradual growth of river-works construction.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the gradual growth of river-works construction.

sentences.zh: 從古無不徙之河，治河惟去其太甚，不必議開議塞，借一勞永逸之辭，為逐利幸功之術。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been a river that did not shift its course; in governing rivers one need only remove the worst excesses, without debating opening or blocking channels, borrowing the language of one effort for lasting benefit as a technique for pursuing profit and courting merit.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity no river has failed to shift its course; governing rivers requires only removing the worst excesses, without debating opening or blocking channels, or using talk of permanent solutions as a pretext for profit and self-promotion.

sentences.zh: 九曰，情罪過當之漸。

translations.literal: Ninth, the gradual growth of disproportion between circumstances and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, the gradual growth of disproportion between circumstances and punishment.

sentences.zh: 如逃人止於鞭刺，過宿反至竄流，輕重不平，枉誣尤甚。

translations.literal: For example, a fugitive slave merits only flogging, yet staying out overnight leads instead to banishment; severity and leniency are unbalanced, and false accusation is especially grave.
translations.idiomatic: A fugitive slave merits only flogging, yet staying out overnight leads to banishment; severity and leniency are unbalanced, and false accusation is especially grave.

sentences.zh: 十曰，積習膠固之漸。

translations.literal: Tenth, the gradual hardening of entrenched habits.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, the gradual hardening of entrenched habits.

sentences.zh: 升遷則趕缺壓缺，處分則忽重忽輕，視為故常，營競特甚。」

translations.literal: In promotion one rushes vacancies and presses down on vacancies; in punishment one is now severe and now lenient—treated as the usual state of affairs, with scheming competition especially intense."
translations.idiomatic: In promotion officials rush vacancies and block rivals; in punishment they are now severe and now lenient—treated as normal, with scheming competition especially intense."

sentences.zh: 复疏論銓政不平，並下部議行。

translations.literal: He again memorialized on the unfairness of appointment policy, and both were sent to the ministries for discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized on unfair appointment policy, and both were sent to the ministries for discussion and implementation.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷奉天府府丞，兼學政。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to be vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture, concurrently serving as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture, concurrently serving as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 轉通政司參議，署通政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a councillor of the Court of Transmission and acted as commissioner of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to councillor of the Court of Transmission and acted as commissioner of transmission.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，病目，卒於家。

translations.literal: When mourning ended his eyes were afflicted by illness, and he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended his eyes failed, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 弘嘉素慎，疏上言過直，輒戰栗。

translations.literal: Hongjia was by nature cautious; when his memorials were too blunt he would tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjia was cautious by nature; when his memorials were too blunt he would tremble.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「子葸若此，何如不言？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "You are so timid—why not simply say nothing?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "You are so timid—why not simply say nothing?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「弘嘉之戰栗，氣不足也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Hongjia's trembling comes from insufficient vital force.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Hongjia trembles because his vital force is insufficient.

sentences.zh: 然知其當言，不敢欺吾心，尤不敢負吾君耳。」

translations.literal: Yet knowing that one ought to speak, I dare not deceive my own heart, and still less dare I fail my sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing one ought to speak, I dare not deceive my own heart, and still less dare I fail my sovereign."

sentences.zh: 高層雲，字二鮑，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Gao Cengyun, courtesy name Erbao, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cengyun, styled Erbao, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of the Kangxi reign (1676).

sentences.zh: 授大理寺評事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a reviewing official of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as a reviewing official in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was appointed a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi (1686), he was made a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，太皇太后崩，詔王大臣集永康左門外議喪禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the Grand Empress Dowager died; an edict ordered princes and grand ministers to assemble outside the Left Gate of Yongkang to discuss mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year (1687), upon the death of the Grand Empress Dowager, the emperor ordered princes and senior ministers to gather outside the Left Gate of Yongkang to deliberate on the funeral ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 大學士王熙等向諸王白所議，跪移時，李之芳年老，起而踣。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Xi and others reported to the princes what had been deliberated, kneeling for a long time; Li Zhifang, being old in years, rose and fell prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Xi and others knelt for a long while as they briefed the princes on the matters under discussion; the aged Li Zhifang stood up only to collapse.

sentences.zh: 層雲曰：「是非國體也。」

translations.literal: Cengyun said: "This is not proper to the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Cengyun declared, "This is an affront to the dignity of the state."

sentences.zh: 即日疏言謂：「天潢貴冑，大臣禮當致敬。

translations.literal: That same day he memorialized, stating: "Members of the imperial clan are exalted by birth; ministers should by ritual show them respect.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he submitted a memorial, stating, "Princes of the imperial blood deserve the respect customarily paid them by ministers.

sentences.zh: 獨集議國政，無弗列坐，所以重君命、尊朝廷也。

translations.literal: But when gathering solely to deliberate on state affairs, none fail to sit in ranks—this is how one honors the sovereign's command and exalts the court.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers meet solely to discuss state policy, however, all sit as equals in session—precisely to honor the emperor's commission and uphold the authority of the court.

sentences.zh: 況永康左門乃禁門重地，太皇太后在殯，至尊居廬，天威咫尺，非大臣致敬諸王之地。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Left Gate of Yongkang is a forbidden gate and a place of grave importance; the Grand Empress Dowager lay in state, the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning quarters, and Imperial Majesty was near at hand—this was no place for grand ministers to pay homage to princes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Left Gate of Yongkang is a restricted inner gate. With the Grand Empress Dowager lying in state and the emperor residing in mourning quarters, the majesty of the throne was close at hand—hardly the setting for grand ministers to prostrate themselves before princes.

sentences.zh: 大學士為輔弼大臣，固當自重，諸王亦宜加以禮節，不可驕恣倨慢，坐受其跪，失籓臣體。」

translations.literal: Grand secretaries are assisting ministers and ought indeed to maintain their own dignity; the princes, too, should observe propriety and not be arrogant, insolent, and haughty, sitting and accepting their kneeling—this would cause them to lose the deportment befitting feudatory princes and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's chief counselors, grand secretaries must uphold their own dignity, and princes should observe proper decorum rather than sit in arrogance accepting such obeisance—conduct unworthy of imperial kinsmen who serve the throne."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上曰：「朕召大臣議事，如時久，每賜墊坐語。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said: "When I summon grand ministers to discuss affairs, if the time is long, I always grant them cushioned seats for conversation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor remarked, "Whenever I summon ministers for extended deliberations, I always provide cushions so they may sit while we speak.

sentences.zh: 今大臣為諸王跪，於禮不合。」

translations.literal: Now for grand ministers to kneel to princes is not in accord with ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: For grand ministers to kneel before princes is a breach of proper ritual."

sentences.zh: 下宗人府，吏、禮二部議，嗣後大臣與諸王會議，不得引身長跪，著為令。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Ministries of Personnel and Rites for deliberation; thereafter, when grand ministers met in conference with princes, they were not permitted to prostrate themselves in extended kneeling—this was established as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Ministries of Personnel and Rites, which ruled that in future meetings between senior ministers and princes, extended kneeling would be forbidden—a regulation thereafter enforced as law.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，京師旱，詔求言。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the capital suffered drought; an edict solicited opinions.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Kangxi (1689), drought struck the capital, and the emperor issued an edict inviting memorials and advice.

sentences.zh: 層雲疏論江、淮間行屯田擾民，請急停蘇民困，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: Cengyun memorialized on the military colonies being established between the Yangtze and Huai rivers harassing the people, requesting that they be urgently halted to relieve the people's distress; the emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Cengyun submitted a memorial decrying how military colony programs along the Yangtze-Huai region were oppressing the populace and urging their immediate suspension to ease popular hardship; the emperor praised and adopted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 遷通政司參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a vice commissioner in the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner in the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷太常寺少卿，卒官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to be a vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1690), he was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, a post in which he died.

sentences.zh: 沈愷曾，字樂存，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Shen Kaiceng, courtesy name Lecun, was a native of Guian in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kaiceng, styled Lecun, was from Guian prefecture in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十六年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of Kangxi (1687) and was chosen for appointment as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 三十年，改山東道御史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was reassigned as a censor on the Shandong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1691), he transferred to serve as inspector on the Shandong circuit of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 喀爾喀率屬內附，上親出塞拊循。

translations.literal: The Khalkha led their followers in submitting to the dynasty, and the emperor personally went beyond the frontier to console and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khalkha Mongols led their tribes in submitting allegiance, the emperor personally journeyed beyond the Great Wall to receive and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 愷曾疏言：「巡行口外，為蒙古諸臣定賞罰，編戶口，安插新附。

translations.literal: Kaiceng memorialized, stating: "The tour beyond the passes is to fix rewards and punishments for the various Mongol ministers, register households, and settle the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiceng memorialized, stating, "The tour beyond the frontier is to fix rewards and punishments for Mongol leaders, register households, and resettle the newly submitted tribes.

sentences.zh: 但聖躬遠出，間關崎嶇，乘輿勞頓於外，群臣晏息於家，臣心何安？

translations.literal: But the sacred person goes far abroad, traversing rugged and perilous routes; the imperial carriage wearies and toils in the wilds, while the multitude of ministers rest at ease in their homes—how can this servant's heart be at peace?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty will travel far into arduous country while your ministers remain at home in comfort—how can I reconcile that in conscience?

sentences.zh: 宜遣部院大臣經理，令逐一奏聞，仍與皇上親行無異。

translations.literal: It is fitting to dispatch grand ministers of the ministries and courts to manage affairs, requiring them to report each item in turn to the throne—the effect would still be no different from the emperor going in person.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers from the ministries and courts should be dispatched to manage these affairs and report each matter to the throne—an arrangement that would achieve the same ends as Your Majesty's personal journey.

sentences.zh: 乞傳旨暫緩此行。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be transmitted to suspend this journey for the time being."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly request that Your Majesty defer this expedition."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, no reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but drew no imperial response.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，召愷曾入對，賜宴。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, he summoned Kaiceng for an audience and bestowed a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, the emperor summoned Kaiceng for a private audience and honored him with a banquet.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，歲暮，以餘孽未靖，復出塞。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan; at year's end, because the remnant rebels had not been pacified, he again went beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year (1696), the emperor marched in person against Galdan; at year's end, with rebel holdouts still unpacified, he returned to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 愷曾复上疏請回鑾，語甚剴切。

translations.literal: Kaiceng again submitted a memorial requesting the emperor's return to the capital; his language was very earnest and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiceng again memorialized urging the emperor to return to the capital, his language strikingly forthright and impassioned.

sentences.zh: 順天學政侍郎李光地有母喪，命奪情視事，光地請給假九月，言路大譁。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Guangdi, educational commissioner of Shuntian, suffered his mother's death; he was ordered to set aside mourning and continue in office; Guangdi requested nine months' leave, and the censorial community erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guangdi, educational commissioner of Shuntian, entered mourning for his mother, the emperor ordered him to leave mourning aside and remain in post; Guangdi's request for nine months' leave provoked an uproar among the memorializing officials.

sentences.zh: 愷曾疏言：「學臣關係名教，表率士子。

translations.literal: Kaiceng memorialized, stating: "The educational commissioner bears upon the fundamental teachings of moral order and serves as a model for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiceng memorialized, stating, "The educational commissioner is charged with upholding moral orthodoxy and setting an example for scholars.

sentences.zh: 使衰絰者衣錦論文，其何以訓？

translations.literal: To have one in hemp mourning garments discuss literature while clothed in brocade—by what means can he instruct?
translations.idiomatic: How can a man in mourning garb preside over literary examinations in full court dress—what lesson would that teach?

sentences.zh: 宜令終喪，以隆孝治。

translations.literal: He should be ordered to complete his mourning period, so as to elevate the governance of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He should be permitted to complete his mourning, thereby honoring the dynasty's ideal of filial governance.

sentences.zh: 閣臣職司票擬，理應委曲奏請，始不當有在任守制之票，既不當有仍遵前旨之擬。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries, whose duty is drafting rescripts, ought properly to present petitions tactfully and thoroughly; from the first there ought not to have been a rescript draft for holding office while observing mourning, and once that was improper, there ought not to have been a draft to continue following the previous edict.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries, whose office is to draft imperial rescripts, should have tactfully petitioned the throne from the outset rather than issuing a draft permitting service while in mourning, and certainly should not later have drafted obedience to the earlier order.

sentences.zh: 科臣職司封駁，閣臣票擬不當，科臣繳旨覆奏，固其職也。

translations.literal: Censorial officials, whose duty is sealing and rejecting, when the grand secretaries' rescript drafts are improper, for censorial officials to return the edict with a memorial of response—this is indeed their office.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials are charged with reviewing and rejecting improper rescripts; when the grand secretaries' draft was wrong, it was their duty to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 乃亦復默然，不知其所謂封駁者何在也？

translations.literal: Yet they likewise remained silent—where, one wonders, is that so-called sealing and rejecting?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they too held their tongues—where, then, was the censorate's vaunted power of remonstrance?

sentences.zh: 臣不敢以妄擬閣臣為嫌，劾奏同列為咎。」

translations.literal: This servant dares not shrink from presumptuously criticizing the grand secretaries out of consideration, nor from impeaching colleagues out of blame-fearing."
translations.idiomatic: I do not hesitate to criticize the grand secretaries or to impeach fellow officials when duty requires it."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下九卿議，尋用彭鵬言，令解任在京守制。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was sent down to the Nine Ministers for deliberation; soon Peng Peng's view was adopted, ordering Guangdi relieved of his post to observe mourning in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Nine Ministers; shortly thereafter the court adopted Peng Peng's recommendation and ordered Li Guangdi to resign his post and observe mourning in the capital.

sentences.zh: 陝西提督孫思克請令富民納粟佐軍，愷曾論奏乞敕部停止，上是之。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Military Governor Sun Sike requested that wealthy households be made to contribute grain to assist the army; Kaiceng submitted a memorial arguing and requesting that the ministry be ordered to halt it; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi Military Governor Sun Sike proposed requiring wealthy households to contribute grain for military supplies, Kaiceng memorialized urging the relevant ministry to halt the scheme, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 入台七年，疏數十上，伉直敢言。

translations.literal: After entering the censorate for seven years, he submitted several tens of memorials, upright and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: During seven years in the censorate he submitted dozens of memorials, distinguished by his forthright and fearless candor.

sentences.zh: 歷掌山西、江南、浙江、河南道事，管登聞院。

translations.literal: He successively supervised the affairs of the Shanxi, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and Henan circuits, and managed the Court of Complaints.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn on the Shanxi, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, and Henan censorial circuits and oversaw the Court of Complaints.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，巡兩廣鹽課，多惠政，商民德之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he inspected the salt levies of the two Guang provinces; there were many benevolent policies, and merchants and common people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year (1699), while inspecting salt administration in Guangdong and Guangxi, he enacted numerous reforms that endeared him to merchants and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 報滿，留任一年。

translations.literal: When his term was reported complete, he was retained in office for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing his term, he was retained for an additional year.

sentences.zh: 還京，复掌山西道。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again supervised the Shanxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, he resumed charge of the Shanxi censorial circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，以廣東運使罣誤事連坐，罷官。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning; because the Guangdong transport commissioner was implicated in a mishandled affair, he was implicated by association and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his father, he was dismissed from office after being implicated in a misconduct case involving the Guangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上南巡，召試行在稱旨，賜御書。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, when the emperor toured the south, he was summoned for examination at the temporary palace and found pleasing to the imperial intent; he was bestowed imperial calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year (1705), during the emperor's southern tour, Kaiceng was summoned for examination at the imperial lodge, distinguished himself, and received the gift of imperial calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 龔翔麟，字蘅圃，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Gong Xianglin, courtesy name Hengpu, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xianglin, styled Hengpu, was from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父佳育，字祖錫。

translations.literal: His father was Jiayu, courtesy name Zuxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Jiayu, styled Zuxi.

sentences.zh: 自龍驤衛經歷出知安定縣，又自兵部郎中出為分巡通永道僉事，擢江南布政使，所至有聲績。
