translations.literal: From a clerk in the Dragon Flying Guard he went out to serve as magistrate of Anding County; again from a director in the Ministry of War he went out as regional inspector of the Tongyong Circuit as an assistant commissioner, was promoted to financial commissioner of Jiangnan, and wherever he went had a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a clerk in the Dragon Flying Guard, he went on to serve as magistrate of Anding County; later, as a director in the Ministry of War, he was posted as regional inspector of the Tongyong Circuit and eventually rose to financial commissioner of Jiangnan, earning distinction at every post.

sentences.zh: 入授光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] and was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 命修賦役簡明書，未竟。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Concise Book of Tax and Corvée Duties; it was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to compile a concise manual on tax and corvée obligations, but the work remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before completing the assignment.

sentences.zh: 翔麟自副貢生授兵部主事，出榷廣東關稅。

translations.literal: Xianglin, from a tribute student, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War and went out to collect Guangdong customs duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin entered service as a Ministry of War secretary after graduating as a tribute student, and was posted to collect Guangdong customs revenue.

sentences.zh: 沿海諸稅口，遠者去省二千里，吏役苛索，商民重困。

translations.literal: Along the coast the various tax stations, the farthest being two thousand li from the provincial capital, had clerks and runners making harsh demands, and merchants and common people were heavily afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal tax stations stretched as far as two thousand li from the provincial capital, where clerks and runners extorted merchants and commoners with crushing severity.

sentences.zh: 翔麟嚴其禁，並移行府縣察究。

translations.literal: Xianglin strictly enforced prohibitions, and moreover circulated instructions to prefectures and counties to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin rigorously enforced prohibitions against such abuses and circulated orders to prefectures and counties to investigate offenders.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十三年，考選陝西道御史，遂疏請以諸稅口交府縣徵收，著為令。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Kangxi he was selected by examination as a censor on the Shaanxi circuit, then memorialized requesting that the various tax stations be handed to prefectures and counties for collection, and this was established as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of Kangxi (1694), after selection as a Shaanxi circuit censor, he memorialized that coastal tax collection be transferred to prefectures and counties—a reform thereafter enacted as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視西城。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to inspect the Western City.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to inspect the Western City district of the capital.

sentences.zh: 大學士熊賜履以誤擬旨罷，復起為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xiong Cilu was dismissed for erroneous rescript drafting, then reappointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xiong Cilu had been dismissed for drafting an erroneous rescript, but was later restored and appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 翔麟疏劾：「賜履竊講學虛聲，前因票擬錯誤，嚼毀草簽，卸過同官。

translations.literal: Xianglin memorialized impeaching: "Cilu trades on a hollow reputation for lecturing on learning; previously because of erroneous rescript drafting, he chewed and destroyed the draft slip, shifting blame onto a colleague.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin impeached him in a memorial: "Cilu cultivates an empty reputation as a scholar-official. When he once drafted a mistaken rescript, he chewed up the draft slip and shifted blame onto a colleague.

sentences.zh: 皇上從寬，放歸田裡。

translations.literal: The emperor showed leniency and sent him home to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed mercy and sent him home to retirement.

sentences.zh: 旋賜起用，晉位冢宰，毫無報稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted reinstatement, promoted to head of the Six Ministries, with not the slightest repayment in service.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and promoted to head of the Six Ministries, yet has shown no gratitude in service whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 其弟賜瓚包攬捐納，奉旨傳問，賜履不求請處分，猶泰然踞六卿之上。

translations.literal: His younger brother Cizan monopolized purchase-of-office donations; by imperial order he was summoned for questioning; Cilu did not request punishment, yet still sat calmly above the six ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Cizan monopolized the sale of offices; when summoned for questioning by imperial order, Cilu made no request for punishment and still sits complacently above the six ministers.

sentences.zh: 乞賜罷斥。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be dismissed and expelled."
translations.idiomatic: I request that he be dismissed from office."

sentences.zh: 右通政張雲翮，故靖逆侯勇子。

translations.literal: Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission Zhang Yunyi was the son of the former Marquis of Pacifying Rebellion Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission Zhang Yunyi was the son of Yong, the late Marquis of Pacifying Rebellion.

sentences.zh: 勇妻李卒，雲翮不居喪。

translations.literal: When Yong's wife Li died, Yunyi did not observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis Yong's wife Lady Li died, Yunyi failed to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 翔麟疏劾：「雲翮縱非李出，嫡母、繼母並製三年，豈可視為陌路？

translations.literal: Xianglin memorialized impeaching: "Even if Yunyi was not born of Li, both birth mother and stepmother require three years' mourning—how can he treat them as strangers on the road?
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin impeached him: "Even if Yunyi was not Lady Li's biological son, both birth mother and stepmother require three years of mourning—how can he treat them as strangers?

sentences.zh: 乞嚴加議處，以儆敗類。」

translations.literal: I beg that severe deliberation and punishment be applied, to warn corrupt types."
translations.idiomatic: I request that he be severely punished as a warning to others who would violate moral norms."

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督趙良棟討吳三桂，定雲南，以敘功未允，為部下乞恩，屢有求請。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Zhao Liangdong campaigned against Wu Sangui and pacified Yunnan; because merit rewards were not granted as he wished, he begged favors for his subordinates and repeatedly made requests.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Zhao Liangdong had suppressed Wu Sangui and pacified Yunnan, but dissatisfied with the merit awards granted, he repeatedly petitioned on behalf of his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 翔麟疏劾：「良棟效力行間，悉由皇上指授方略。

translations.literal: Xianglin memorialized impeaching: "Liangdong's service in the field was entirely directed by the emperor's assigned strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin impeached him: "Liangdong's battlefield service owed entirely to strategies assigned by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 蕩平後敘功，既經廷議，重以睿裁，輕重無不允當。

translations.literal: After pacification merit was assessed; having gone through court deliberation and further weighed by imperial judgment, none of the gradations were not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, merit awards were deliberated in court and confirmed by imperial judgment—every rank was fairly assigned.

sentences.zh: 事閱十年，而良棟猶嘵嘵不已，妄肆薦揚，市恩於眾，借矜己功。

translations.literal: The matter had passed ten years, yet Liangdong still clamored unceasingly, recklessly promoting and praising, currying favor with the multitude, borrowing to boast of his own merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years have passed, yet Liangdong still clamors on, recklessly promoting favorites, currying popular favor, and boasting of his own achievements.

sentences.zh: 且越例求賜莊田、房屋，言詞狂悖，大不敬。

translations.literal: Moreover he transgressed precedent seeking gifted estate fields and houses; his words were wild and insolent, grossly disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: He has further transgressed precedent by demanding gifted estates and houses, his language wild and insolent—gross disrespect to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乞下所司定罪。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be sent down to the relevant office for conviction."
translations.idiomatic: I request that the appropriate authorities determine his punishment."

sentences.zh: 賜履雅負清望，良棟功臣，雲翮功臣子，翔麟論列無所避，以是得直聲。

translations.literal: Cilu had long enjoyed a pure reputation, Liangdong was a meritorious minister, and Yunyi was a meritorious minister's son—Xianglin criticized them without avoidance, and thereby gained a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cilu enjoyed a long-standing reputation for integrity, Liangdong was a meritorious general, and Yunyi the son of one, Xianglin criticized them all without hesitation and thereby earned a reputation for upright candor.

sentences.zh: 俄又劾賜履及侍郎趙士麟亂銓政，條列以上。

translations.literal: Soon he again impeached Cilu and Vice Minister Zhao Shilin for corrupting appointment administration, itemizing and submitting above.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he again impeached Cilu and Vice Minister Zhao Shilin for corrupting the appointment system, submitting a detailed bill of particulars.

sentences.zh: 官御史十年，乞歸，貧至不能舉火，蕭然不改恆度。

translations.literal: After ten years as censor he requested retirement; he was so poor he could not kindle a fire, yet in desolate simplicity he did not alter his constant bearing.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years as a censor he retired; though so poor he could scarcely afford fuel, he maintained his austere integrity unchanged.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 高遐昌，字振聲，河南淇縣人。

translations.literal: Gao Xiachang, courtesy name Zhensheng, was a native of Qi County in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiachang, styled Zhensheng, came from Qi County in Henan.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年進士，授湖南龍陽知縣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Longyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Kangxi (1676), he was appointed magistrate of Longyang County in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以屯賦重，請減與民田同額。

translations.literal: Because military colony levies were heavy, he requested a reduction to the same amount as civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: Finding military colony taxes excessively burdensome, he petitioned to reduce them to the same rate as civilian farmland.

sentences.zh: 父憂去。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he departed office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補廣東東莞知縣，歷茂名、信宜，護高州知府，皆有聲。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was assigned as magistrate of Dongguan in Guangdong; he served in Maoming and Xinyi and acted as prefect of Gaozhou—all with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was posted as magistrate of Dongguan in Guangdong, later served in Maoming and Xinyi, and acted as prefect of Gaozhou, earning a good reputation at each post.

sentences.zh: 行取，擢刑部主事，累遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: Selected for capital service, he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Justice and successively transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for service in the capital, he rose from secretary in the Ministry of Justice to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was appointed a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year of Kangxi (1707), he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時提督九門步軍統領託合齊恃權不法，給事中王懿德列款疏劾。

translations.literal: At the time Tuoheqi, military governor and commander of the Nine Gates Infantry, relied on power and acted unlawfully; Supervising Secretary Wang Yide listed items in a memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tuoheqi, commander of the Nine Gates Infantry, abused his authority unlawfully; Supervising Secretary Wang Yide submitted a detailed impeachment memorial against him.

sentences.zh: 上方幸熱河，遐昌詣行在繼劾之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then sojourning at Rehe; Xiachang went to the temporary palace and continued impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at his Rehe retreat, Xiachang traveled to the imperial lodge and submitted a follow-up impeachment.

sentences.zh: 略言：「託合齊欺罔不法，經懿德糾參，臣又何敢置喙？

translations.literal: He stated in summary: "Tuoheqi has deceived and acted unlawfully; since Yide has already impeached him, how would this servant dare insert a word?
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in summary: "Tuoheqi has deceived the throne and broken the law; since Wang Yide has already impeached him, what more can I add?

sentences.zh: 伏念其所以橫恣，皆緣握權太過。

translations.literal: Reflecting humbly, the reason for his tyrannical arrogance is entirely that he wields power to excess.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I submit that his tyranny stems entirely from excessive concentration of power in his hands.

sentences.zh: 自督捕裁，而所轄三營改歸提督，悍將驕兵，毫無忌憚。

translations.literal: Since the office of Chief Pursuit and Capture was abolished, the three battalions under its jurisdiction were transferred to the military governor; fierce generals and arrogant soldiers have not the slightest scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Chief Pursuit office was abolished and its three battalions placed under the infantry commander, fierce generals and arrogant soldiers have acted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 請仍歸兵部擇司官督率，考勤惰、禁勒索，營務防汛，晝夜巡邏，即有姦匪，不得妄牽無辜，私刑酷訊。

translations.literal: I request that they again be returned to the Ministry of War, with selected bureau officials to supervise and lead, checking diligence and idleness, prohibiting extortion; garrison duties and flood defense, patrolling day and night along the walls—even if there are criminal bandits, innocent persons must not be recklessly implicated, nor privately tortured in harsh interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The battalions should be returned to Ministry of War supervision, with bureau officials appointed to monitor discipline, forbid extortion, manage garrison and flood-defense duties, and patrol the walls day and night—so that even when criminals are at large, innocents are not arbitrarily detained or tortured in private interrogations.

sentences.zh: 提督干預詞訟，奸民構弁兵，擇人而噬，民不聊生。

translations.literal: The military governor interferes in lawsuits; wicked commoners frame sergeants and soldiers, choosing people to devour; the people cannot sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: The commander interferes in civil litigation, while unscrupulous citizens frame soldiers against their enemies; the populace can scarcely survive.

sentences.zh: 請仍歸大、宛二縣，五城司坊、巡城御史以及府尹、治中。

translations.literal: I request that [such matters] again be returned to the two counties of Daxing and Wanping, the ward officers of the Five Cities, the wall-patrol censors, and the prefect and vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Civil jurisdiction should be restored to the counties of Daxing and Wanping, the Five Cities ward officers, the wall-patrol censors, and the metropolitan prefect and vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 逃盜命案，歸於刑部，一秉國法。

translations.literal: Cases of fugitives, bandits, and homicides should be returned to the Ministry of Justice, uniformly upholding the laws of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving fugitives, bandits, and homicide should fall under the Ministry of Justice, to be adjudicated uniformly under national law.

sentences.zh: 提督管理街道，縱其兵丁肆為貪噬，勢壓官民。

translations.literal: The military governor manages the streets, indulging his soldiers and runners in unrestrained greedy devouring; his power presses down on officials and common people.
translations.idiomatic: Street administration under the infantry commander has allowed soldiers to plunder freely, their power overwhelming both officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 請五城分治，仍歸司坊。

translations.literal: I request that the Five Cities divide governance, again returning [authority] to the ward officers.
translations.idiomatic: Street governance should be divided among the Five Cities and restored to the ward officers.

sentences.zh: 每年工部保題司官督理，庶法官守制，無復軼越。

translations.literal: Each year the Ministry of Works should nominate and propose bureau officials to supervise management, so that legal offices observe their jurisdictions and there is no further transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Ministry of Works should nominate supervising officials, so that each agency respects its proper jurisdiction and no further overreach occurs.

sentences.zh: 此皆本朝舊例，當歸所司，防微杜漸，不致成積重之勢。」

translations.literal: These are all old precedents of this dynasty; they should be returned to the relevant offices, nipping evil in the bud and stopping gradual encroachment, so that it does not become a situation of accumulated weight."
translations.idiomatic: These were all established precedents of our dynasty; restoring them to their proper agencies would check abuses early and prevent power from accumulating beyond control."

sentences.zh: 疏上，上以巡捕三營併步軍統領，非自託合齊始。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said that merging the three pursuit battalions under the infantry commander was not something that began with Tuoheqi.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor replied that consolidating the three pursuit battalions under the infantry commander predated Tuoheqi's tenure.

sentences.zh: 司坊管街道，畏懼顯要，止知勒索鋪戶，故亦歸併步軍統領。

translations.literal: The ward offices managed the streets but feared the powerful and only knew how to extort shopkeepers, and therefore street administration was also merged under the infantry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Ward offices managed the streets but feared the powerful and only extorted shopkeepers, so street administration was merged under the infantry commandant as well.

sentences.zh: 今既累商民，即以遐昌兼管，期一年責以肅清。

translations.literal: Now that merchants and people had suffered enough, Xiachang was put in concurrent charge, with a deadline of one year to bring order.
translations.idiomatic: Now that merchants and people had suffered enough, Xiachang was put in concurrent charge, with one year to restore order.

sentences.zh: 遐昌既任事，革除陋規，街道溝渠次第平治，兵民以安。

translations.literal: Once Xiachang took office he abolished corrupt practices; streets and drains were put in order in succession, and soldiers and civilians were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiachang took office he abolished corrupt practices; streets and drains were put in order, and soldiers and civilians lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 兩屆報滿，仍命接管。

translations.literal: After two terms' reports were complete, he was still ordered to continue in charge.
translations.idiomatic: After two terms he was still ordered to continue in charge.

sentences.zh: 託合齊陰圖報復，欲伺隙中傷。

translations.literal: Tuoheqi secretly plotted revenge and wished to seize an opening to wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoheqi secretly plotted revenge and watched for a chance to strike at him.

sentences.zh: 五十年，上自暢春園還，見內城街道被侵占甚窄，召託合齊詰責之。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, when the emperor returned from the Garden of Everlasting Spring he saw that inner-city streets had been encroached upon until very narrow and summoned Tuoheqi to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year, returning from the Garden of Everlasting Spring, the emperor saw inner-city streets narrowed by encroachment and summoned Tuoheqi to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 託合齊奏外城尤窄。

translations.literal: Tuoheqi memorialized that the outer city was even narrower.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoheqi reported that the outer city was even narrower.

sentences.zh: 命尚書赫碩色等察勘，託合齊故引視僻巷，民居佔官街得三百餘間，謂皆遐昌任內所造，逮下刑部獄。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister Hesose and others to inspect; Tuoheqi deliberately led them to view secluded alleys, finding more than three hundred dwellings occupying official streets, claiming all were built during Xiachang's tenure, and had him arrested and sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minister Hesose and others to inspect; Tuoheqi deliberately led them through secluded alleys, found more than three hundred dwellings encroaching on official streets, claimed all were built during Xiachang's tenure, and had him sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison.

sentences.zh: 尚書齊世武，託合齊黨也，將刑訊，主事蔣晟持不可。

translations.literal: Minister Qishiwu was of Tuoheqi's faction and was about to apply torture in interrogation; director Jiang Sheng objected that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Qishiwu, a member of Tuoheqi's faction, was about to torture him in interrogation; director Jiang Sheng objected.

sentences.zh: 乃議遐昌以官街邀民譽，應發奉天安置。

translations.literal: They then debated that Xiachang had used official streets to win popular praise and ought to be sent to Fengtian for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: They then argued that Xiachang had used official streets to win popular praise and ought to be sent to Fengtian for resettlement.

sentences.zh: 託合齊黨复譁，言遐昌受賂。

translations.literal: Tuoheqi's faction again clamored, saying Xiachang had taken bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoheqi's faction clamored again, claiming Xiachang had taken bribes.

sentences.zh: 嚴訊家屬，定爰書，謂據供雖未受賂，但風聞街道舊規，鋪戶修房，每間與胥役錢二三百，以此例之，房三百餘間，計錢七百五十千，當枉法贓律處絞。

translations.literal: His family was strictly interrogated and the case record fixed, stating that though confession did not show he had taken bribes, it was heard that by old street regulations shopkeepers repairing houses gave clerks two or three hundred cash per room; by this reckoning, for more than three hundred rooms the total was seven hundred fifty thousand cash, and he ought to be executed by strangulation under the statute on illicit gain through bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: His family was strictly interrogated and the case record fixed: though confession showed no direct bribes, by old street practice shopkeepers paid clerks two or three hundred cash per room when repairing houses; for more than three hundred rooms that totaled seven hundred fifty thousand cash, warranting strangulation under the statute on illicit gain through bending the law.

sentences.zh: 朝審，具冤狀。

translations.literal: At court review he presented a statement of wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: At court review he presented a statement of wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 尚書王掞、李天馥謂遐昌廉能為上知，宜從寬典，富寧安讚之，獄乃緩。

translations.literal: Ministers Wang Yan and Li Tianfu said Xiachang's integrity and ability were known to the emperor and he ought to receive lenient treatment; Funing'an praised this, and the case was slowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Wang Yan and Li Tianfu said the emperor knew Xiachang's integrity and ability and he ought to receive lenient treatment; Funing'an agreed, and the case was slowed.

sentences.zh: 會託合齊以病乞假，隆科多攝其職，因言託合齊罔上行私，橫恣貪婪，及誣陷遐昌狀。

translations.literal: When Tuoheqi begged leave on grounds of illness, Longkodo took over his duties and reported that Tuoheqi had deceived the throne and pursued private ends, acted violently and was greedy, and described how he had framed Xiachang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoheqi begged sick leave, Longkodo took over his duties and reported that Tuoheqi had deceived the throne, pursued private ends, acted violently and greedily, and had framed Xiachang.

sentences.zh: 上命釋遐昌，都人爭赴獄舁之出，擁赴闕謝。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xiachang released; capital residents rushed to the prison to carry him out and escorted him to the palace gate to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xiachang released; capital residents rushed to the prison to carry him out and escorted him to the palace gate to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 及出都，送者填溢，醵金完懸贓。

translations.literal: When he left the capital, senders filled the roads; they pooled money to pay off the suspended illicit-gain fine.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the capital, well-wishers filled the roads and pooled money to pay off the suspended illicit-gain fine.

sentences.zh: 遐昌歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Xiachang returned home and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiachang returned home and died before long.

sentences.zh: 論曰：康熙間以直言著者，魏象樞、郝浴、楊素蘊、彭鵬、趙申喬輩，敭歷中外，卓然為名臣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Among those famed in the Kangxi era for blunt speech were Wei Xiangshu, Hao Yu, Yang Suyun, Peng Peng, Zhao Shenqiao, and others, who served inside and outside the court and stood out as renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Among those famed in the Kangxi era for blunt speech were Wei Xiangju, Hao Yu, Yang Suyun, Peng Peng, Zhao Shenqiao, and others, who served at court and in the provinces and stood out as renowned ministers.

sentences.zh: 希轍、縉，自世祖朝巳在諫垣，有獻替。

translations.literal: Xizhe and Jin had been in the remonstrance offices since the Shizu reign and offered constructive counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhe and Jin had served in the remonstrance offices since the Shunzhi reign and offered constructive counsel.

sentences.zh: 弘嘉論十漸，層雲爭國體，陳義皆甚高。

translations.literal: Hongjia discussed the ten gradual deteriorations, Cengyun contended for national dignity—the principles they advanced were all very lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjia discussed the ten gradual deteriorations and Cengyun contended for national dignity—the principles they advanced were all lofty.

sentences.zh: 若德格勒、紫芝、重光忤明珠，愷曾彈李光地，翔麟論熊賜履、趙良棟，遐昌抗託合齊，雖所糾繩賢不肖不同，謇謇匪躬，不為名懾，不為勢撓，謚為「遺直」，殆無愧歟？

translations.literal: As for Degele, Zizhi, and Chongguang, who offended Mingzhu; Kaiceng, who impeached Li Guangdi; Xianglin, who criticized Xiong Cilu and Zhao Liangdong; and Xiachang, who resisted Tuoheqi—though those they reproved differed in worth, they were all upright and devoted to duty, unafraid of reputation and unbowed by power; styled "Remaining Upright," they can scarcely be said to have fallen short of that title, can they?
translations.idiomatic: Degele, Zizhi, and Chongguang offended Mingzhu; Kaiceng impeached Li Guangdi; Xianglin criticized Xiong Cilu and Zhao Liangdong; Xiachang resisted Tuoheqi—though their targets differed in worth, all were upright and devoted to duty, unafraid of reputation and unbowed by power; styled "Remaining Upright," can they scarcely be said to fall short of that title?
